home.title: Fifty – Mölkky Game with a daily puzzle
home.description: Throw the stick, knock down the pins and land on exactly 50. A new puzzle every day, the same for everyone. No account, works offline.
home.heading: Fifty – Mölkky Game
intro: Fifty is a throwing game with the rules of Mölkky. Drag, aim and release: the stick slides into the pins, or flies over the front ones with a lob. One pin scores its number, several score their count, and going over 50 drops you back to 25.
Every day brings one new puzzle, the same for every player: reach exactly 50 in as few throws as you can. Then practise as much as you like, or play a full game from the starting formation.
**[Play the daily puzzle in your browser](https://haraltti.github.io/molkkygame/play/)**, no installation needed.
home.storesNote: The app is on its way to the App Store and Google Play.

features.title: A daily puzzle
features.text: One new layout a day, the same for everyone. You get one attempt, and a goal to beat.

features.title: Two throws
features.text: A low throw slides along the ground. A lob flies over the pins in front and lands where you aim.

features.title: Real Mölkky scoring
features.text: Exactly 50 wins, over 50 drops to 25, and three misses in a row end the game. Fallen pins are stood up where they slid to.

features.title: Streak and sharing
features.text: Keep your streak of solved days going and share your result as a short text.

features.title: No account
features.text: No sign-up and no login. Your results stay on your phone.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: The puzzles are made on your phone, so you can play without a connection.

items.name: Fifty – Mölkky Score Keeper
items.text: Playing real Mölkky in the yard? Tap the fallen pins and the app keeps the score and follows the rules.

privacy.heading: Privacy policy
privacy.description: How the Fifty – Mölkky Game app handles data: no accounts, data stays on your device, ads through Google AdMob, consent choices and how to delete your data.
intro: This policy explains what the Fifty – Mölkky Game app (“the app”) does with information. We have kept the app simple on purpose: there are no user accounts, and we do not run a server that collects your data.
The game can also be played in a web browser at haraltti.github.io/molkkygame/play. The browser version shows no ads and collects no data: your results are stored only in your browser.

ul: No user accounts and no sign-up.
Your daily puzzle results, settings and background picture are stored only on your device.
The app is free and shows ads through Google AdMob. Google processes some data to show and measure ads (see below).
In Europe the app asks for your consent first, and on iPhone it may also ask for tracking permission.
The app is not directed at children under 13.
Deleting the app deletes all the data the app has stored.

p: The app stores the following only on your phone. We cannot see it and it is never uploaded:
ul: the daily puzzles you have played (your throws, the result and your streak),
your settings (language, theme, accent colour, vibration, ad consent state),
a background picture, if you choose one. You pick it with the system’s photo picker, and the app keeps a private copy inside its own storage.

p: The app is free and is supported by ads. The ads are provided by Google AdMob (Google). To show, measure and protect ads, Google may collect and use:
ul: device identifiers, such as the advertising ID,
your IP address and the approximate location derived from it,
usage and diagnostic information about the app and the ads, such as ad views and interactions, device model and operating system version.
after: Google collects and processes this data under its own policies. We do not receive it; we only see summary statistics such as the number of ad impressions. Read more in [How Google uses information from sites or apps that use its services](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites) and in the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).
The ads appear as a banner on the game screen, as a full-screen ad after a game and as an ad when the app is opened. No ad is ever shown in the middle of a throw.

p: In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and other regions where the law requires it, the app shows Google’s consent form (UMP, User Messaging Platform) before the first ad is requested. Your choice decides whether ads may be personalised.
You can review or change your choice at any time in the app: **Settings → Ads and privacy → Ad privacy settings** (shown where consent applies).

After the consent form, the app may ask for permission to track you across other companies’ apps and websites (Apple’s App Tracking Transparency). If you say no, you can still use the whole app and you still see ads, but they are not personalised using that kind of tracking.
You can change this later in iOS **Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking**, or in the app’s own settings page in iOS Settings.
On Android you can reset or delete your advertising ID, and opt out of ad personalisation, in your phone’s settings (usually under Privacy → Ads).

The app can receive updates to its code over the air through Expo’s EAS Update service. When the app starts, it contacts Expo’s servers to check for an update. Like any internet connection, this reveals technical information to Expo, such as your IP address, platform and app version. We do not receive personal information through this. See the [Expo privacy policy](https://expo.dev/privacy).

The app is meant for the whole family but is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. The app tells Google that it is not child-directed and limits ads to content rated PG or milder.
If you think a child has given us personal information, contact us and we will help.
We do not keep your data on a server, so there is nothing for us to delete. Deleting the app from your phone removes all results, settings and the background picture.
Data that Google holds for ads is managed in your Google Account, in [My Ad Center](https://myadcenter.google.com/).

Because we do not process your personal data ourselves, requests about data used for ads should be made to Google, which acts as an independent controller for it. For anything else, you can contact us and we will answer you.
If the app changes in a way that affects your data, we will update this page and the date at the top.
Publisher and data controller: Harri Heikkilä, Finland. Questions about privacy: {email}.

support.heading: Support
support.description: Help for the Fifty Mölkky game: how to throw, scoring, the daily puzzle, what happens to your results when you change phones, and ad privacy settings.
intro: Answers to common questions about the Fifty Mölkky game. If you do not find yours, write to us.

a: Drag down on the playing field and release. The direction of the drag sets where the stick goes and its length sets the power. The dotted line shows the path up to the first hit.
Choose **Lob** to throw over the pins in front: the ring shows where the stick lands.
The scoring follows the rules of Mölkky:
ul: If you knock down one pin, you score the number on it. If you knock down two or more, you score the number of pins that fell.
Exactly 50 points wins. If you go over 50, your score drops back to 25.
Three misses in a row end the game. A scoring throw resets the count.
Fallen pins are stood up where they slid to, so every throw changes the field.

faq.q: Why can I play the daily puzzle only once?
a: The daily puzzle is the same for everyone, so everyone gets one attempt. Your throws are saved as you play, and the puzzle continues from where you left it if you close the app. **Practice** and **Full game** can be played as often as you like.

faq.q: What is the goal shown in the puzzle?
a: It is a number of throws that solves the puzzle, found by the app. It is something to aim for, not a limit: a good throw can beat it.

faq.q: Does the app need an internet connection?
a: No. Everything works offline, including the how-to-play guide. An internet connection is only used to show ads and to check for app updates.

faq.q: What happens to my results when I change phones?
a: There is no account and no cloud sync, so the app does not move your data to a new phone by itself. Results, the streak and settings are stored only on the device.
If you restore a full backup of your old phone (iCloud or Google backup), the app’s data may come along, depending on your backup settings. Otherwise you start fresh on the new phone.

faq.q: How do I change my ad privacy settings?
a: Open **Settings → Ads and privacy** in the app. Where consent applies (for example in the EU), there is an **Ad privacy settings** button that reopens Google’s consent form.

On iPhone you can also change the tracking permission in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking. On Android you can reset your advertising ID in your phone’s settings. See the [privacy policy](page:privacy) for details.

faq.q: How do I delete my data?
a: Delete the app from your phone. All results, settings and the background picture are removed with it.

faq.q: The text does not fit or something looks wrong.
a: Please tell us which phone and language you use, and what you saw. A screenshot helps.
